title: Tech stocks rebound as Nasdaq rises 1% and the Dow slips in early trading
text:

Computing Consumer Tech Space & Aerospace Earnings Menu Money & Markets Economic Indicators Markets Personal Finance Earnings Menu Lifestyle Cars & Bikes Collecting Entertainment Food & Fine Dining Health and Fitness Real Estate Travel Markets Tech stocks rebound as Nasdaq rises 1% and the Dow slips in early trading
 The S&P 500 gained 0.5% as Intel, AMD and Micron stock advanced following a 4.5% weekly drop in the Nasdaq
 By Cris Tolomia · 2 min read · Updated October 19, 2026 Add QZ to Google Smith Collection / Gado / Getty Images
 The Nasdaq $NDAQ Composite gained 1% in early Monday trading, with investors buying technology shares again after the AI-driven sell-off the previous week.
 The S&P 500 gained 0.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.1%.
 Intel $INTC stock gained 5% on an upgrade from JPMorgan $JPM , and CoreWeave stock rose 4% once Goldman Sachs $GS raised its recommendation, according to CNBC . Shares of Advanced Micro Devices and Micron $MU Technology each gained 3%.
 The Nasdaq fell 4.5% last week, ending a four-week winning streak. The S&P 500 suffered its steepest one-week loss since the end of June, and the information technology sector endured its roughest stretch since April 2025, according to CNBC. The sector lost more than 6%.
 CoreWeave stock shed over a quarter of its value last week amid worries about its debt, the steepest weekly decline for the shares since November 2025, according to CNBC. Credit default swaps on the company's debt have reached distress levels, according to CNBC.
 CNBC, citing unnamed sources, reports that Anthropic brought in $16.8 billion during the third quarter, compared with $11.6 billion in the second quarter. The figures prompted investors to question how fast AI spending will keep growing.
 "AI Credit Spreads and hyperscalers specifically are at the widest levels of the year," Goldman Sachs traders said in a note, according to CNBC.
 Oil prices slipped on Monday. Brent crude fell 1.9% to $107.73 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate traded near $100, down 1%. Attacks on ships in the Persian Gulf have become more frequent, and Ukraine and Russia have exchanged strikes on energy facilities. Ukraine struck a terminal for oil in the Russian city of St. Petersburg on Sunday.
 Longer-dated oil futures are now rising, reflecting a market expectation that problems at energy facilities will persist into 2027, according to CNBC.
 European stock indexes traded lower, while French government debt weakened following weekend violence at cost-of-living protests nationwide, according to The Wall Street Journal . The yield on France's 10-year government bond rose to 4.887%, and the euro slipped against the dollar.
 Earnings reports from major companies, including Meta $META Platforms and Tesla $TSLA , are scheduled this week, according to CNBC.
